what: GEO-NOW (2026-10-24): the PR818 study's three models -- the global head, the query-aware head and the attention baseline -- on this branch's tensor unit, against main's (level 2, GEO-2b's builds) in one process with every trained state and logit the same bytes, and against PyTorch at fixed shapes; and two of the step's levers measured and not taken: THP-0 (the attention's buffers on transparent huge pages), WADJ-ROWS-0 (the weight adjoints' row ranges small enough for sixteen tasks) and KBK-0 (the k-blocked kernel's 448-term block in L1-sized sub-ranges). The first runs of geo_ab.py and geo_compare_static.py shared the cores with a micro-benchmark for some seconds; they were set aside and both rerun with nothing else running. Records only: no runtime change.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz, 4 vCPU (AVX-512F, AMX), 2 MiB of L2 a core, 260 MiB of L3; Linux 6.18 (transparent huge pages: madvise); GCC 13.3 (the overlays' builds); clang 18 (the attention and GEMM libraries); Python 3.11, NumPy 2.2.6, torch 2.13.0+cu130 (CPU); OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE
